## What this does

Plumbing, not part of the method itself. Looks up a site or species code
in a sorted list and returns its position (or 0 if not found), using
binary search so this stays fast even with millions of records — e.g. the
2 038 000 bryophyte records across 3695 sites used in the paper's example
(Hill 2011, p.196). Every time the code needs to relate a record to "which
site is this" or "which species is this", it goes through `binfnd`.

```{.rust filename="src/lib.rs" tangle="lib__binfnd"}
pub fn binfnd(ma: &[Name], n: usize, na: &Name) -> usize {
    let mut imin = 1usize;
    let mut iamin = ma[imin];
    let mut imax = n;
    let mut iamax = ma[imax];
    loop {
        if imax - imin <= 1 {
            if iamin == *na {
                return imin;
            }
            if iamax == *na {
                return imax;
            }
            return 0;
        }
        let imid = (imax + imin) / 2;
        let iamid = ma[imid];
        if *na <= iamid {
            imax = imid;
            iamax = iamid;
        } else {
            imin = imid;
            iamin = iamid;
        }
    }
}
```
